statement: Copyright vests initially in the author; work by an employee within the scope of employment is a work made for hire owned by the employer, but a commissioned work from an independent contractor is a work made for hire only if it falls within the nine categories enumerated in 17 U.S.C. § 101 (software is not one) and the parties expressly agreed in a signed writing, so companies take contractor-created code by written assignment under § 201(d) (17 U.S.C. § 101, § 201(a), (b), (d)).
caveat: A contractor agreement without an express present-tense assignment clause leaves the copyright with the contractor regardless of payment. State law governs the contract mechanics. This repo does not review specific agreements.
reviewer: Lane editorial review (law-map 2026-10-14); independent domain expert review pending
